name: Weekly Cisplatin Concurrent with Radiation (Cervical Cancer Chemoradiation)
histology: cervical squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or adenosquamous carcinoma

biomarkers.note: Single-agent cisplatin as a radiosensitizer is not biomarker gated. PD-L1 (combined positive score) testing is recommended for recurrent, progressive, or metastatic disease to guide later immunotherapy, not this concurrent chemoradiation. Pembrolizumab may be ADDED to cisplatin (or carboplatin)/RT for FIGO 2014 stage IIIA to IVA (category 1) per CERV-F, handled in a separate protocol.

lineOfTherapy: primary (definitive) treatment of locally advanced cervical cancer; radiosensitizing chemotherapy given concurrently with external-beam radiation therapy (EBRT) followed by brachytherapy

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: locally advanced cervical carcinoma treated with definitive chemoradiation (EBRT plus brachytherapy)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, primary treatment pathways; footnote (Concurrent platinum-containing chemotherapy with EBRT utilizes cisplatin as a single agent, or carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate renal function for cisplatin with hydration
eligibilityCriteria.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 170910 to 170911 (cisplatin alone, weekly at a dose of 40 mg/m2, concurrent with external-beam radiation; the weekly-cisplatin schedule used in most GOG studies is the most frequently recommended standard)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 170910 to 170911. CISplatin 40 mg/m2 IV once weekly, given concurrently with external-beam radiation therapy. DeVita notes this weekly schedule is preferred over every-3-week cisplatin (50 to 75 mg/m2) plus 5-FU because of less severe acute hematologic and GI toxicity. Requires pre- and post-infusion hydration; carboplatin is substituted if cisplatin intolerant (NCCN footnote). Tall man per ISMP.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration and antiemetics
premedications.notes: IV hydration before and after cisplatin; antiemetic prophylaxis for the platinum agent.

supportiveCare: cisplatin hydration protocol (pre- and post-infusion) to reduce nephrotoxicity.
monitor for radiation-plus-chemotherapy additive acute toxicity (skin, GI, hematologic).

monitoring: CBC before each weekly cisplatin dose
renal function (creatinine, electrolytes including magnesium) before each weekly dose
audiometry/otologic and peripheral-neuropathy assessment for cisplatin oto- and neurotoxicity
weekly review of concurrent radiation acute toxicity

doseModificationRules.condition: rising creatinine, electrolyte derangement, or grade 2+ cisplatin toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold weekly cisplatin or switch to carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant per NCCN footnote; physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 170909 to 170914 (chemoradiation trials used cisplatin alone weekly at 40 mg/m2, or cisplatin 50 to 75 mg/m2 plus 5-FU every 3 weeks; weekly cisplatin emerged as the most frequently recommended standard)

guideline.locator: Systemic Therapy for Cervical Cancer, Chemoradiation, single-agent Cisplatin (or Carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant) (CERV-F 1 of 4); primary-treatment concurrent-chemotherapy footnote

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for weekly single-agent cisplatin concurrent with radiation, the standard radiosensitizing chemotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer (StewardMD reference disease cervical_cancer, subtype #42). CISplatin 40 mg/m2 IV weekly is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. lines 170910 to 170911, which identify weekly cisplatin as the most frequently recommended standard concurrent with external-beam radiation. Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Cervical Cancer v2.2026 (CERV-F) confirms concurrent platinum-containing chemotherapy with EBRT uses cisplatin as a single agent (or carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant) but does not print a per-dose number. cycleLengthDays 7 (weekly) is sourced; the number of weekly doses (typically given across the EBRT course) is NOT concretely stated in the cited sources, so regimen.cycles is set to VERIFY and listed in verifyFields. Cisplatin requires hydration with nephro-, oto-, and neurotoxicity monitoring. Tall man per ISMP. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
